properties.decision: Chosen: reflow2 itself stamps the server time on every node's creation and on each change to its content, from now on; a stamp sent by a caller is refused. The order of a prediction and the result that tests it is read from those stamps and SAID ("stated before the result", "stated after the result (post hoc)", "revised after the result"), never enforced: a late prediction is not refused and no support/refute reading changes because of order. A node written before stamping began reads "order not recorded"; a stamp carried in by an import or design copy reads "imported, not recorded here" unless the export's hash chain vouches for it. Rejected: flo2.io answering from its gateway write log (hosted only, from 2026-09-23, outside reflow2's read-back); both (two pieces to keep agreeing); park it (only caller-typed dates remain).
properties.name: The order of prediction and result is read from server-recorded times, and said, never enforced
properties.rationale: Measured 2026-10-28 on reflow2 main 73b29e4 (gap-3 agent, measure-first step): reflow2 records NO server-side time or order for a node's creation or content change. The store saves only caller properties; every dated property (created_at, reported_at, detected_at, AUTHORED_BY authored_at/approved_at from acted_at) is caller-typed; Snapshots keep prior wording but carry no time; the server clock is read only for search ages, id minting, the usage ledger (no node ids) and sidecars. The one time a caller cannot set is flo2.io's Postgres design_writes.created_at, outside reflow2. So the proposed option (a), "read server-recorded times", had nothing to read; Anthony chose the new stamp. Anthony's word 2026-10-28, AskUserQuestion: "reflow2 stamps writes (Recommended)".
